text:
nina: Noticed eu-west racks showing persistent warm-pool fragmentation. Top offenders have heavy cross-region egress to us-east which stops allocator from coalescing.
sam: Confirmed on telemetry: warm_slice_count up ~40% vs baseline and cross-region bytes spiked. Likely driving capacity inefficiency and cost.
raj: Telemetry snapshot: high KV-churn + lots of small long-lived sessions (~10-20m) with outbound to us-east-s3. Allocator treats them as incompatible for packing.
nina: Short-term mitigation idea: host-level egress shaping per-tenant to prevent link saturation + a light proxy to localize S3 for noisy tenants. Then enable an allocator coalesce canary that respects egress-locality labels.
mike: For shaping we used simple tbf in staging: 
```
# cap tenant egress to 300mbit
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 300mbit burst 32k latency 400ms
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -m comment --comment "tenant:123" -j MARK --set-mark 123
```
sam: Allocator policy patch (sketch): 
```
coalesce:
  enable: true
  max_slot_size: 4
  require_egress_local: true
```
raj: Plan: canary in rack eu-west-1a. Steps: 1) tag top noisy tenants with egress_local=true, 2) deploy DaemonSet to apply shaping for those tenants, 3) deploy s3-rewrite proxy canary, 4) flip allocator feature flag in that rack. Monitor warm_slices, cross_az_bytes, token latency.
deploy-bot: @nina scheduled-canary: "egress-localize-euw1a" -> start Thu 08:00 UTC for 24h. Infra PR required for allocator feature flag.
mike: I'll build DaemonSet image and emit metrics: tenant_egress_bps, tenant_egress_shaped_bps.
sam: Add alerts: sudden increase in p99 token latency or >10% rise in inter-rack bytes -> rollback.
nina: Owners: sam -> allocator PR & feature-flag gate, mike -> DaemonSet + metrics, raj -> dashboards and tenant-tagging. Keep updates here.
raj: Pushed dashboard panel draft and a query for cross_region_egress_by_tenant.
mike: Image pushed: registry/internal/egress-shaper:canary1. Logs look good in staging.
sam: I'll open PR 9001 and include unit tests and a soft rollback trigger.
nina: Thanks. If cost spikes while canary is running ping ops and we'll pause.
